text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday: NEUE ZUERCHER ZEITUNG - Member of the Swiss lower house of parliament elected Judith Stamm, member of the Christian Democratic fraction, as its new president. - The number of over-night stays in Swiss hotels dropped in October by 6.5 percent to 2.25 million. - Swiss-Swedish group ABB received two orders worth a total of 383 million Swiss francs to build two power plants in South Korea and Indonesia. TAGES ANZEIGER - Delegates of the Jewish World Congress in Oslo welcomed the investigations that Switzerland has begun to find unclaimed funds in Swiss bank accounts. - Two Swiss customs investgation officers were arrested on Friday, who were allegedly involved in a bribery scandal. JOURNAL DE GENEVE - Export of Swiss pilot trainer airplanes 'Pilatus', which can be modified into fighter jets, will become more difficult as the Swiss government is now allowed to restrict export when delivered to a country that was placed under an embargo by the UN or another major trade partner. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
